slot.brief: solve a first-order linear ODE dy/dx + P(x)y = Q(x) after identifying and applying the integrating factor

stem: The general solution of the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y \sec^2 x = \tan x \sec^2 x$ is

verdicts.working: Integrating factor: e^{∫sec²x dx}=e^{tan x}. Then (ye^{tan x})'=tan x sec²x e^{tan x}; integrating gives ye^{tan x}=e^{tan x}(tan x−1)+C, hence y=tan x−1+Ce^{−tan x}.

working:
Linear in $y$: $P(x)=\sec^2 x$, $Q(x)=\tan x \sec^2 x$.  
I.F. $= e^{\int \sec^2 x\,dx} = e^{\tan x}$.  
Multiply: $\frac{d}{dx}\bigl(y e^{\tan x}\bigr) = \tan x\,\sec^2 x\, e^{\tan x}$.  
Let $u=\tan x$, $du = \sec^2 x\,dx$: $\int u e^u\,du = (u-1)e^u + C$.  
Hence $y e^{\tan x} = (\tan x - 1)e^{\tan x} + C \;\Rightarrow\; y = \tan x - 1 + Ce^{-\tan x}$.

Independent check: Integrating factor: e^{∫sec²x dx}=e^{tan x}. Then (ye^{tan x})'=tan x sec²x e^{tan x}; integrating gives ye^{tan x}=e^{tan x}(tan x−1)+C, hence y=tan x−1+Ce^{−tan x}.
solution:
For the linear equation, the integrating factor is $e^{\int \sec^2 x\,dx}=e^{\tan x}$. Thus
$$\frac{d}{dx}\bigl(ye^{\tan x}\bigr)=\tan x\sec^2x\,e^{\tan x}.$$
Let $u=\tan x$; integrating gives $ye^{\tan x}=(u-1)e^u+C$, hence $y=\tan x-1+Ce^{-\tan x}$.
